card.title: Director of Operations
card.description:
**About the role**

**Krosswood Doors** builds residential interior and exterior doors in Tucson, Arizona, and sells them through The Home Depot and Krosswood.com. We build doors mostly one at a time, through manual and semi-automated processes, against a daily target of 400+ doors and lead times under three days.

The **Director of Operations** is the top plant leader in Tucson and owns every function and transaction at the site, from receiving raw material to shipping quality doors on time. The job: consistently deliver safe, high-quality products, on time, at the lowest sustainable cost, while developing people and building scalable systems. At our size, that means deep involvement in daily operations while building the organization for future growth.

You will partner closely with the SVP Operations on both daily execution and priorities. The SVP owns multi-year strategy, final budget and capital approval, the ERP roadmap and the executive relationship with The Home Depot. You will be the leader on the floor and the site’s main point of contact for every stakeholder.

**How we run the plant**

* Daily success: a steady and consistent flow of great doors, built safely and efficiently, with uncompromising quality. The system you will run and improve:
* Daily accountability system: production hard-start, morning stand-up, QA meeting, hourly board walks and daily close-out, backed by Leader Standard Work for every manager.
* Total Ownership: every process, machine, tool, task and space has one named owner and a documented standard.
* SQDC-P scoreboards: safety, quality, delivery, cost and people results by station, with a first pass yield (FPY) target of 95% or better.
* 6S and visual management: 6S (5S plus safety) at every station, standard work, operator and machine cards.
* Escalation: operator to lead in under 5 minutes, to manager in under 15, to Director of Operations in under 30, and to the SVP Operations in under 60.

**What you’ll do**

* Operational leadership: own the daily production plan and schedule, capacity planning, staffing, equipment and resource allocation; manage the hour-by-hour KPIs, remove bottlenecks and lead daily issue resolution.
* Safety: own safety culture, compliance, training, reporting, audits and corrective actions; make sure the daily safety cross is completed and every issue is resolved.
* Operational excellence: run and improve the production management system (daily and weekly accountability rhythms and KPIs); drive documented standard work, visual management, Lean, 6S, kaizen and labor utilization.
* Quality: build and own the quality management system: documented quality standards, FPY, escape prevention, defect reduction and root cause and corrective action, working with the Quality & Process Specialist.
* Delivery: drive throughput, flow and on-time delivery to homedepot.com; avoid and mitigate Home Depot fines; manage releases, PPR and duration exceptions; lead ERP (NetSuite) improvements with IT.
* Cost: own labor and material cost, labor utilization and budget adherence; align staffing, temp labor and overtime with sales volume; build capital (CAPEX) proposals and a continuous cost-improvement program.
* People: build an engaged culture; run performance management (reviews, scorecards, discipline), recognition, staffing and wages; develop your managers into leaders; own training and succession planning for direct labor.
* Warehouse: own inventory and transaction accuracy, documented SOPs and adherence, PPR and order management, staffing, material shortages and cost savings.
* Analysis: make data-based decisions; build system-based tools and KPIs; dig into the details to find wins, losses, risks and opportunities.
* Cross-functional: work with sales, purchasing, IT and finance to resolve issues and improve quality, delivery, cost and the customer experience; handle HR issues and site administration.
* Process knowledge: know each process well enough to spot when an operator, machine or function falls short of the expected result, then lead root cause analysis and corrective action.

**What you’ll bring**

Required

* 10+ years of manufacturing operations leadership in a high-mix, low-volume, custom or craft setting, including leading managers across production, warehouse and maintenance.
* Proven success implementing and sustaining Lean, 5S/6S and Kaizen.
* Has built and run a production management system: daily and weekly accountability rhythms, KPIs and visual management.
* Has built or improved a quality management system, with measurable gains in first pass yield and defect reduction.
* Owned an operating budget and built capital spending proposals; manages labor, temp staffing, overtime and material cost.
* Strong data skills: builds KPIs and reports, and uses data to find root causes and make decisions.
* Hands-on HR experience: performance reviews, discipline, wage adjustments, hiring and leadership development.
* Experience writing, enforcing and training SOPs and process documentation.
* Fluent in English and Spanish, able to communicate clearly with the whole workforce.
* Able to separate a process breakdown from process noncompliance, and respond to each the right way.
* A confident, hands-on leader with the discipline to hold the line and the patience to build people up.
* Bachelor’s degree in operations management, industrial engineering, engineering or business, or equivalent experience.

Preferred

* NetSuite or other ERP experience, including leading ERP improvements (strongly preferred).
* Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt.
* Preventive maintenance or TPM knowledge.
* Safety management and OSHA compliance experience.
* Wood products, doors, millwork, cabinetry or finishing background.
* Experience meeting retailer or e-commerce delivery requirements, such as The Home Depot.

**How success is measured**

Timeframe

* First 30 days - Knows every station and function; runs the daily accountability system alongside the SVP Operations; has met each manager one-on-one; understands the budget
* First 90 days - Runs the site independently; Leader Standard Work followed at every station; top 3 throughput, quality and cost losses named with action plans; 12-month improvement plan agreed with the SVP Operations
* Ongoing - 400+ doors a day at 95%+ FPY; zero lost-time injuries; on-time delivery with no fines; labor and material cost on budget; managers leading their areas on their own; systems that scale with growth

**Work environment and benefits**

This is a 100% on-site, floor-first role in an active manufacturing plant with machinery, noise, wood dust and finishing materials. PPE is provided and required.

**Benefits**: Medical, dental, 401(k), PTO and more

**Salary:** $72,000–$85,000 per year, based on experience, plus 10% annual bonus

card.title: Operations Director
card.description:
**Overview**

As an Operations Director, you’ll lead business operations with a focus on strong financial performance, reliable service, and continuous improvement. You’ll connect strategic planning with day-to-day execution, using data to guide decisions and align teams around clear priorities. Your impact: By improving processes and coordinating operational and sales priorities, you help employees work effectively and customers receive consistent service.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead operations management, business management, and strategic management across teams; set priorities and monitor progress against business goals.
* Oversee financial management, including profit and loss (P&L) analysis, budgeting, and Excel data analysis to support data-driven decision making.
* Direct project management and process improvement initiatives; apply lean management principles to reduce inefficiencies and strengthen operational management.
* Guide sales and business development efforts in partnership with relevant leaders, connecting customer service insights to business priorities.
* Provide executive-level team management, managerial communication, and team leadership; supervise, coach, and develop managers and employees.

**Qualifications**

* Demonstrated leadership, management, and supervising experience in operations or business settings.
* 12+Experience with team management, team development, and strategic planning, including translating goals into practical plans.
* Working knowledge of profit and loss, financial management, and Excel data analysis; able to use information to make sound business decisions.
* Skills in project management, operational management, process improvement, and customer service.
* Ability to communicate clearly with executives and teams and collaborate on sales and business development priorities.

Pay: $13,000.00 - $180,000.00 per year

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible schedule
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance

card.title: Director of Business Systems & Operations
card.description:
About the Company

CCS / Orange Tape operates a multichannel business encompassing direct-to-consumer ecommerce, wholesale distribution, and Amazon marketplaces. Our portfolio includes CCS, Alien Workshop, and Habitat Skateboards. We are an entrepreneurially minded, creatively ambitious company focused on operational excellence and continuous improvement.

Founded in 1985, CCS is one of the most recognized names in skateboarding and streetwear. For generations, the CCS catalog helped shape skateboarding culture, introducing millions of customers to new brands, products, artists, and ideas. Today, CCS is a digital-first retailer and apparel brand, combining a deep history in skateboarding with a focus on creating compelling products and connecting with the next generation of customers. Alien Workshop and Habitat Skateboards, two iconic skateboarding brands, are operated through Orange Tape, our wholesale distribution business.

We are based in Portland, OR, with 50+ employees.

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly analytical, technically capable Director of Business Systems & Operations to help improve how our business operates through better systems, stronger analysis, and effective execution.

Working closely with our CEO, CIO, and department managers, this individual will identify opportunities to improve business performance, develop internal applications and reporting tools, and take responsibility for a variety of operational and administrative initiatives.

The position combines business analysis, operations management, and technology-enabled process improvement. Responsibilities range from developing tools to improve reporting and inventory planning to analyzing shipping costs, evaluating operational productivity, and negotiating vendor agreements.

We are particularly interested in candidates who combine strong business judgment and analytical skills with technical aptitude and the ability to develop practical solutions. Traditional software engineering experience is not required. We place greater value on intellectual curiosity, initiative, operational understanding, and demonstrated success solving business problems.

This is a hands-on position for someone who enjoys both analyzing problems and taking responsibility for getting things done.

Key Responsibilities

* Business Systems Development: Design, build, and maintain internal applications, reporting tools, and automated workflows supporting merchandising, purchasing, inventory management, finance, fulfillment, and other functions
* Business & Operational Analysis: Analyze sales, inventory, margins, shipping costs, labor productivity, and other operating metrics to identify problems, recommend improvements, and support management decisions
* Business Operations: Support and improve operations across CCS and Orange Tape, including evaluating performance, identifying inefficiencies, resolving cross-functional issues, and ensuring effective execution of key initiatives
* Inventory Planning: Support inventory planning, purchasing budgets, forecasting, and open-to-buy processes, working with buyers and other employees to improve inventory productivity, availability, and working capital efficiency
* Vendor & Cost Management: Evaluate vendor performance and costs, assist with shipping carrier and other vendor negotiations, and identify opportunities to improve service and reduce expenses
* Reporting & Decision Support: Develop tools that improve access to operational and financial information, automate repetitive reporting, and help employees analyze data and make better decisions
* Technology & Systems Projects: Work closely with our CIO on NetSuite, Shopify, systems integrations, data infrastructure, and other technical initiatives, including projects supporting ecommerce operations
* Administrative Oversight: Supervise the HR/Office Manager, including payroll review and approval, insurance administration, and related responsibilities
* Operational Improvement & Execution: Identify opportunities to improve business processes and own selected projects from initial analysis through implementation, testing, and employee adoption

Qualifications

Required:

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant professional experience
* 4+ years of relevant experience in business operations, business systems, business analysis, finance, inventory planning, ERP systems, or related functions
* Hands-on experience with NetSuite, including a strong understanding of its business processes, data, and reporting capabilities
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret business and financial information and develop practical recommendations
* Strong business and financial acumen, including an understanding of profitability, inventory management, operating costs, and the financial implications of business decisions
* Strong Excel skills and general technical proficiency, including the ability to use technology to develop practical business solutions
* Ability to work across departments, coordinate projects, negotiate with vendors, and take responsibility for operational results
* Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, initiative, and the ability to manage multiple priorities independently

Preferred:

* Experience in ecommerce, retail, wholesale distribution, consumer products, or another inventory-intensive business
* Experience in accounting, financial analysis, financial systems, or operations analysis
* Experience with NetSuite administration, consulting, reporting, saved searches, or workflows
* Experience with inventory forecasting, open-to-buy planning, or operational performance management
* Experience using AI tools, such as Claude Code, ChatGPT, or similar platforms, to develop applications, automate workflows, analyze data, or solve business problems
* Experience developing internal applications, reporting tools, or business process automations
* Familiarity with Shopify, Amazon, and multichannel business operations
* Experience improving operational efficiency, implementing business applications, or negotiating vendor and service agreements

Compensation

$110,000 - $160,000 per year, depending on experience

Benefits

* Flexible schedule
* Paid time off
* 401(k)
* Employee discount on merchandise
* Catered lunch every other week

Pay: $110,000.00 - $160,000.00 per year

card.title: Operations Director
card.description:
Mercantile Development, Inc. (MDI) is a leading independent converter of nonwoven wiping products, proudly family-owned and operated for over 75 years. As a WBENC-certified Women’s Business Enterprise, we are driven by a commitment to quality, innovation, and customer-focused service. Our Pro-Series® professional-grade wiping products are manufactured in our 140,000 sq. ft. state-of-the-art facility in Shelton, Connecticut under an ISO 9001:2015 certified Quality Management System and distributed worldwide across diverse industries.

At MDI, we value innovation, collaboration, accuracy, and integrity. We are proud to foster a workplace culture that encourages creative problem-solving, continuous improvement, and strong team relationships.

Mercantile Development is seeking a hands-on Operations Director to lead all aspects of site operations and oversee a small team. You will hold direct responsibility for the daily management of the facility, including production, warehousing, engineering, maintenance, and the grounds and infrastructure of the property. The role requires active involvement in every operational area to keep the site safe, efficient, well maintained, and profitable, while consistently meeting customer requirements, quality standards, production goals, and business objectives. This is a full-time, onsite position for a seasoned manufacturing leader who is comfortable running the daily operation and independently driving the projects, facility improvements, and initiatives that move the business forward.

**Job Responsibilities**

· Own the day-to-day running of the Shelton site, setting priorities and standards across every department and holding department leads accountable for safety, quality, delivery, and cost results.

· Coordinate scheduling and resource decisions among departments, working with the Production Supervisor to keep customer commitments and site capacity in balance.

· Establish and review site-wide KPIs, including equipment utilization, labor efficiency, downtime, waste, and inventory flow, and drive corrective actions and continuous improvement.

· Safeguard the site's physical assets, including production equipment, utilities, building systems, and rooftop solar installations, through preventive maintenance, inspections, and timely repairs.

· Develop the site's long-range facility and capital plan, then lead CAPEX projects from budgeting and vendor selection through startup and results validation.

· Working knowledge of OSHA regulations and safe manufacturing practices, and a passion for building a workplace where safety comes first.

· Manage vendor and contractor relationships, maintenance spending, and operating budgets to control costs and maximize value.

· Promote accountability, workforce development, and root-cause problem solving across the organization.

· Update executive leadership regularly on performance, risks, staffing, facility issues, and capital needs.

**Requirements**

· 7+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership, including accountability for output and direct supervision of teams.

· Proven track record running plant equipment, buildings, and preventive maintenance programs, and delivering capital projects within budget while working with outside vendors and contractors.

· Solid grounding in production planning, capacity and workforce planning, equipment reliability, quality systems, and Lean or process-improvement methods.

· Familiarity with ISO 9001:2015 is a plus.

· Strong interpersonal, communication, project management, organizational, and financial acumen.

· Bachelor’s degree preferred in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related discipline; equivalent experience will be considered.

**Benefits**

MDI offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

· Company-paid medical coverage for employees

· Life insurance

· Voluntary vision coverage

· Paid vacation time

· Paid holidays

· Profit-sharing plan

· On-site fitness facility available at no cost to employees

**Physical Requirement**

· Position requires constant walking or standing for an 8 + hour shift

· Must be able to lift and carry heavy items as needed

· Ability to move with ease around manufacturing equipment

Pay: $140,000.00 - $160,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Life insurance
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Experience:

* manufacturing leadership: 7 years (Required)

Work Location: In person

* Experience developing business opportunities, proposals, scopes, cost estimates, pricing, and managing service contracts and commercial risks.
* Strong knowledge of treatment operations, asset reliability, safety, environmental compliance, and emergency response; installation or construction management experience preferred.
* Strong leadership, communication, and technical and commercial judgment; proficiency with business, project, and maintenance management systems.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, environmental science, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant leadership experience considered.
* Applicable California operator certification or professional credential preferred; any certified operator-in-charge duties require the credential mandated for that facility.
* Regular site travel, including Gilroy, Fullerton, and other locations; overnight travel and response to escalated emergencies outside normal hours as required.

Lead and grow an established business unit, develop its people, expand service offerings, and directly influence N2W’s strategic direction, client success, and profitability.

card.description:
**Location**: Detroit, MI 48202 
**Job Type**: Full-Time 
**Schedule:** Primarily weekdays, with flexibility for evenings, weekends, holidays, and emergency response as needed 
**Salary:** $65,000–$75,000 annually 
**Work Location:** On-site

**About Michigan Science Center** 
The Michigan Science Center (Mi-Sci) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to inspiring curiosity and a lifelong passion for science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). Through interactive exhibits, educational programs, and hands-on experiences, Mi-Sci connects people of all ages with science in an engaging and welcoming environment.

**Position Overview** 
The Michigan Science Center is seeking an experienced, hands-on Director of Facility Operations to oversee the daily operations, maintenance, safety, and overall readiness of its facility. 
Reporting to the Managing Director of Experience, the Director of Facility Operations will be responsible for managing building systems, preventive maintenance, contractors, safety procedures, and facility improvement projects. This position requires a proactive leader who can balance long-term planning with day-to-day operational needs. 
The ideal candidate has strong technical knowledge of commercial building systems, experience managing vendors and maintenance operations, and the ability to respond effectively to facility-related issues in a busy, public-facing environment.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Oversee daily facility operations, ensuring the building remains safe, functional, and ready for staff and visitors.
* Manage and monitor building systems, including HVAC, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, building automation, elevators, and other essential infrastructure.
* Develop and maintain preventive maintenance schedules, inspections, work orders, and equipment service records.
* Coordinate and supervise maintenance, custodial, and specialized contractors, ensuring timely and quality service.
* Manage facility operating budgets, service contracts, repair priorities, and capital improvement planning.
* Oversee building safety, security, emergency preparedness, fire and life safety systems, and regulatory compliance.
* Respond to facility emergencies, equipment failures, and operational concerns, coordinating repairs and communicating updates to relevant teams.
* Supervise facility personnel and contractors, providing clear direction, accountability, and support.
* Collaborate with internal departments to coordinate building access, events, maintenance activities, and operational needs.
* Support building opening and closing procedures, including occasional evenings, weekends, holidays, and Manager on Duty (MOD) assignments.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum of 5 years of progressively responsible experience in commercial, institutional, museum, campus, or similar complex facility operations.
* At least 2 years of supervisory, contractor management, or facilities leadership experience.
* Working knowledge of commercial HVAC, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, and building maintenance systems.
* Experience coordinating preventive maintenance, repairs, contractors, and service schedules.
* Ability to assess operational issues, prioritize repairs, and coordinate appropriate technical support.
* Strong communication, organizational, leadership, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to work on-site and respond to occasional after-hours facility needs.
* Associate degree, technical diploma, apprenticeship, relevant professional training, or equivalent substantial experience in facilities management or a related field.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Facilities Management, Engineering, or a related field.
* Experience managing building automation systems, fire and life safety systems, and facility operating budgets.
* Previous experience working in museums, educational institutions, or other public-facing facilities.
* Relevant certifications such as Certified Facility Manager (CFM), Facility Management Professional (FMP), OSHA safety training, or EPA Section 608 certification.

**What We Offer** 
**Salary:** $65,000–$75,000 annually, based on qualifications and experience. 
**Benefits Include:** 
401(k) 
Health, dental, and vision insurance 
Life insurance 
Paid time off (PTO) 
Employee assistance program (EAP) 
Flexible spending account (FSA) 
Health savings account (HSA)

**Equal Employment Opportunity** 
Michigan Science Center is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, national origin, citizenship status, disability, race, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, public assistance status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Michigan Science Center encourages candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply. Applicants who may not meet every listed qualification but believe their skills and experience make them well-qualified are also encouraged to apply.

Pay: $65,000.00 - $75,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Vision insurance

Application Question(s):

* How many years of experience do you have in commercial, institutional, or complex building facility operations?
* How many years of experience do you have supervising facility staff, managing contractors, or leading maintenance operations?
* Do you have hands-on experience overseeing commercial HVAC, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, or building automation systems?
* Are you able to work on-site in Detroit, MI, and accommodate occasional evenings, weekends, holidays, and emergency calls as needed?

Education:

* Associate (Preferred)

Ability to Commute:

* Detroit, MI 48202 (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

card.description:
Job Overview

The Operations Director will oversee the company's day to day operations and work closely with leadership to ensure that business objectives are being met. This role is responsible for managing operational performance, supporting department managers, improving internal processes, and making sure teams have the direction and resources they need to do their jobs effectively.

You will work across finance, sales, customer service, and project management to keep business activities organized and running smoothly. The right person understands how to manage people and resources, keep an eye on financial performance, and address operational problems before they affect the business.

Responsibilities

Oversee daily business operations and work with department managers to establish priorities, assign responsibilities, and maintain consistent performance across teams.

Monitor profit and loss performance, review operating expenses, and work with finance to manage budgets and improve financial results.

Use financial reports, operational data, and Microsoft Excel to evaluate performance, identify problems, and support day to day business decisions.

Manage operational projects and process improvement initiatives, looking for practical ways to reduce unnecessary costs, improve efficiency, and strengthen service delivery.

Work with sales, business development, and customer service teams to coordinate activities and ensure that operational priorities support the company's business goals.

Review existing procedures and introduce improvements where needed, including the use of lean management principles to improve workflow and resource utilization.

Manage and support department managers, provide clear direction, and follow up on operational responsibilities and performance.

Work with senior leadership on business planning, resource allocation, and decisions that affect the company's operations and long term development.

Address operational challenges, resolve internal coordination issues, and ensure that important projects and business activities stay on track.

Experience and Qualifications

Demonstrated experience in operations management, business management, or a related management position, with a strong record of supervising teams and overseeing daily business activities.

Experience managing department managers, coordinating multiple business functions, and maintaining accountability across an organization.

Strong understanding of financial management, profit and loss oversight, operating budgets, and financial performance analysis.

Ability to interpret financial reports, analyze operational data, and use Microsoft Excel to support business decisions.

Experience with strategic planning, project management, process improvement, and operational performance management.

Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to guide managers, develop employees, and address business challenges.

A practical understanding of sales operations, business development, and customer service.

Familiarity with lean management principles and continuous improvement practices is valuable.

Good organizational skills, sound business judgment, and the ability to manage competing priorities while keeping teams focused on results.

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Employee discount
* Flexible schedule
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Parental leave
* Professional development assistance
* Referral program
* Retirement plan
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

**Position Overview**

As His Glory continues to expand its global television network and digital media presence, we are seeking an experienced, strategic and hands-on Director of Television Strategy & Operations to lead initiatives focused on network growth, operational excellence and long-term scalability.

card.title: Director of Operations
card.description:
**Position summary**

The Director of Operations builds and leads the infrastructure that allows Fathers, Families, & Healthy Communities (FFHC) to deliver its programs and services with excellence while growing sustainably. As a member of the leadership team, the Director of Operations oversees all operational functions: human resources, facilities, information technology and systems, and marketing and communications. The role also works closely with finance and program through a dotted-line relationship.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys building and establishing structure. FFHC is at an inflection point: growing its team, strengthening its systems, and preparing for a future office and community space expansion. The Director of Operations will turn that growth into disciplined structure by establishing the policies, procedures, tools and accountability systems that set FFHC apart and free leadership and program staff to focus on the mission.

**Key responsibilities:**

**Operational Leadership & Infrastructure (25%)**

* Serve as a member of the leadership team, contributing to organizational strategy, annual planning, budgeting, and decision-making.
* Lead operational priorities in FFHC's strategic plan and track progress against organizational infrastructure goals and KPIs.
* Design, document, and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs) and workflows across all operational functions, with clear owners and accountability.
* With the Executive Director, build organizational structure and capacity plans that support growth, including role definitions and projected staffing for future years.
* Develop and maintain an organizational risk management and crisis response plan.
* Monitor and oversee organizational insurance policies.
* Support and oversee organizational RFP processes when needed for vendors (audit, managed, IT, insurance, etc.)
* Prepare operations reports and dashboards for the Executive Director and Board of Directors.

**Human Resources & Culture (25%)**

* Oversee all HR functions, including recruitment, hiring, onboarding, offboarding, benefits administration, payroll coordination and personnel records, in partnership with FFHC's PEO (Justworks).
* Ensure compliance with federal, state and local employment laws, including the classification of W-2 employees and contractors.
* Develop and maintain the employee handbook, HR policies, job descriptions and compensation structure.
* Lead the performance management process, including goal setting, quarterly check-ins and annual reviews.
* Develop staff professional development, leadership training, and succession plans that build institutional knowledge.
* Promote a healthy, accountable organizational culture, including staff engagement, wellness and burnout prevention.
* Oversee the intern program's administrative structure, including liaising with universities for contracting, agreements, and onboarding.

**Finance & Administration, dotted line to Finance (10%)**

* Partner with finance leadership on the annual budget, quarterly financial reporting, cash flow planning and audit preparation.
* Manage operational budgets for facilities, technology, HR, and marketing.
* Ensure financial controls and procedures are followed, including purchasing, expense reimbursement, and operational vendor payments.
* Support grant budgets, financial compliance, and reporting requirements in coordination with finance and development staff.
* Help manage banking relationships, including a line of credit, insurance coverage, and organizational contracts.

**Information Technology & Systems (15%)**

* Serve as the main point of contact for FFHC’s managed IT service provider, working closely with the main vendor representative.
* Oversee FFHC's organization-wide technology systems, including Salesforce, SharePoint and Microsoft 365, and other organizational platforms.
* Lead data governance, security, privacy and access-control procedures to protect participant and organizational information.
* Manage IT vendors and contractors, hardware and software inventory, licensing and user accounts in partnership with the managed IT service provider.
* In partnership with the managed IT service provider, develop staff technology training and ensure systems are used consistently across teams.
* Identify opportunities to automate workflows and improve efficiency.

**Facilities (10%)**

* Oversee FFHC's office and program spaces, including leases, maintenance, safety, security and vendor relationships.
* Lead planning and project management for FFHC's future office and community gathering space, including site selection, build-out and move logistics.
* Ensure workplaces meet health, safety and accessibility requirements.

**Marketing & Communications (15%)**

* Oversee FFHC's marketing and communications strategy, brand standards and messaging, in partnership with the Executive Director.
* Manage the website, social media, newsletters and outreach materials, directly or through staff, contractors and agencies.
* Lead production of FFHC's annual Impact Report and other organizational publications.
* Coordinate communications that support fundraising, program recruitment, events and community engagement.

**Supervisory responsibilities**

* Supervises operations staff, contractors and vendors across HR, IT, facilities and marketing.
* Works closely with the Director of Programs and finance leadership to align operational support with program and financial needs.

**Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications**

* 7–10 years of progressive experience in nonprofit operations, administration or management, including at least 3 years in a leadership or supervisory role.
* Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, public administration, business administration or a related field.
* Demonstrated experience building operational infrastructure in a growing organization: policies, SOPs, systems and accountability structures.
* Strong working knowledge of HR practices and employment law, including hiring, performance management, benefits and compliance.
* Experience overseeing technology systems and vendors, including a PEO platform Experience managing facilities, leases or office operations.
* Experience overseeing marketing or communications work, directly or through contractors.
* Availability for some evening and weekend organizational and program events.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in nonprofit management, public administration, business administration or a related field.
* HR certification (SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP or PHR).
* Experience managing budgets and partnering with finance on budgeting, reporting and audits.
* Experience with Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, Microsoft 365 administration or a PEO such as Justworks.
* Experience leading an office relocation or facility build-out.
* Experience in an organization with a $1M–$5M budget during a period of growth.
* Experience with risk management, crisis planning or organizational compliance.
* Familiarity with workforce development, violence prevention, fatherhood or family-serving programs.
* Lived experience in, or strong ties to, the communities we serve.

**What it takes to succeed**

* **Builder's mindset:** you see an organization's potential and create the systems and structures to reach it.
* **Strategic and hands-on:** you can shape long-term plans in a leadership meeting and fix an immediate problem the same afternoon.
* **Operational excellence:** you hold yourself and others to high standards of discipline, consistency and follow-through.
* **Systems thinking:** when a problem repeats, you build a process so it doesn't happen again.
* **Attention to detail:** you catch errors in policies, budgets, contracts and data before they become problems.
* **People leadership:** you develop staff, give clear and honest feedback, and build a culture where people do their best work.
* **Sound judgment and discretion:** you handle confidential personnel, financial and participant information with care.
* **Clear communication:** you explain policies and decisions clearly to staff, leadership, the board and partners.
* **Calm under pressure:** you stay steady during transitions, crises and competing priorities.
* **Collaboration:** you build strong partnerships with program, development, finance and leadership colleagues.
* **Empathy and cultural humility:** you understand the community context of our work and lead with respect.
* **Accountability:** you own outcomes, flag problems early and keep your commitments.

**Physical requirements and work environment**

* Primarily office-based, with regular travel to program sites, partner locations and potential facility sites in Chicago.
* Ability to lift and carry supplies and equipment up to 25 pounds.
* Some evening and weekend hours for organizational and program events; schedule flexibility is offered in return.

Pay: From $85,000.00 per year

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

Education:

* Master's (Preferred)

Experience:

* Operations: 3 years (Preferred)

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Chicago, IL 60616

**Job Title:** Operations Director **Exemption Status/Test:** Exempt

**Reports to:** Superintendent of Schools

Primary Purpose:

Direct and manage district’s maintenance, transportation, and custodial operations. Ensure safe and efficient operation of transportation department. Oversee maintenance of all district-owned vehicles. Maintain physical school plant in excellent operating condition so that full educational use may be made at all times. Provide a physical environment that is functional, safe, clean, and attractive.

Qualifications:

Education/Certification:

Clear and valid Texas commercial driver’s license with Passenger (P) and School Bus (S) endorsements

Special Knowledge/Skills:

Ability to direct and manage operations of school buses and operations inventory 
Knowledge of basic principles of construction, school plant maintenance, and custodial operations

Ability to pass U.S. Department of Transportation alcohol and drug tests and annual physical exam

Knowledge of energy management and vehicle repair and maintenance

Ability to conduct on-site inspections of all vehicle repair and maintenance operations

Ability to manage budget and personnel

Ability to implement policy and procedures

Ability to interpret data and learn transportation routes

Ability to use technology to plan, operate, monitor, and evaluate transportation operations

Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills

1-3 years’ supervisory experience in transportation and maintenance operations

1-3 years’ experience as a bus driver

1. Ensure district facilities are functional, safe, clean, and well maintained.

2. Develop and maintain written departmental procedures for maintenance, repair, and operations of all district buildings and equipment. Ensure work orders are processed and executed in a timely manner.

3. Prepare plans and specifications for contracted repair work and site improvement for submission to purchasing department for bids.

Transportation and Vehicle Maintenance Operations

4. Manage the delivery of transportation services for students and ensure they are picked up and arrive safely and on time.

5. Oversee preparation and updating of bus routes and schedules for all schools in district and develop plans to meet future transportation needs.

6. Communicate changes in routes and scheduling to campuses and the public when warranted.

7. Coordinate transportation for extracurricular activities and special programs.

8. Assign bus drivers to routes and extracurricular trips and find substitutes as needed.

9. Monitor fuel deliveries and distribution.

10. Oversee repair of all district-owned vehicles and preventive maintenance. Ensure vehicle repair requests and work orders are prioritized and processed in a timely manner. Contract for outside services that cannot be performed in shop.

Policy, Reports, and Laws

11. Implement federal and state law, State Board of Education rule, and board policy.

12. Compile, maintain, file, and present all reports, records, and other documents required.

13. Prepare, process, and maintain all documents required to verify safety certification and alcohol and drug testing of bus drivers.

14. Ensure employee time records are accurately maintained and data necessary to process transportation payroll is delivered in a timely manner.

15. Follow district safety protocols and emergency procedures.

Budget and Inventory

16. Develop and administer budget based on documented needs and ensure operations are cost effective and funds are managed wisely.

17. Maintain current inventory of supplies and parts and initiate purchases in accordance with budgetary limitations and district policies. Approve and forward invoices for transportation to accounting department.

18. Recommend disposal of obsolete or worn out vehicles and equipment. Recommend purchase of vehicles as necessary.

Student Management

19. Implement district’s student discipline policies and ensure expectations about appropriate behavior when using district transportation are communicated to students. Enforce student discipline and suspension of riding privileges for any student who violates rules and regulations.

20. Investigate reported concerns and take appropriate action to resolve issues.

Personnel

21. Select, train, supervise, and evaluate staff and make recommendations relative to assignment, retention, discipline, and dismissal.

Safety

22. Enforce safety standards that conform with state, federal, and insurance regulations and develop a program of preventive safety.

23. Ensure equipment is maintained in optimum operating condition.

24. Maintain safety standards in conformance with federal, state, and insurance regulations and district requirements and develop a program of preventive safety.

25. Assess road conditions and hazards and advise administration about inclement weather conditions that may result in delayed starts or the closing of schools.

26. Investigate school bus accidents and student safety violations.

27. Maintain safety standards in conformance with federal, state, and insurance regulations.

28. Organize and conduct training programs to promote a safe work environment.

29. Ensure transportation equipment is in excellent operating condition.

30. Follow district safety protocols and emergency procedures.

Other

31. Participate in development of the district’s disaster plan and be prepared to take an active role in responding to emergencies as needed.

32. Operate bus and district vehicles as needed.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

Supervise, evaluate, and recommend the hiring and firing of maintenance and transportation employees

**About TASKA:**

TASKA Prosthetics produce award-winning multi-articulating myoelectric prosthetic hands - a complex blend of technology, design and engineering that has established itself as an international market lead.

The product is only one part of the company - at TASKA Prosthetics we are deeply committed to our values and foster a culture of care, collaboration, courage and excellence. Our ambition to innovate and challenge the status quo drives us forward and we are continually growing. As we establish a new operational hub in Salt Lake City, we are looking for an experienced Head of Operations to build and lead the operational capability supporting our growth across the United States and wider Americas region.

**About the Role:**

This is an exciting opportunity to join the team at TASKA Prosthetics as the Head of Operations for our newly established USA operational hub. Reporting to the Commercial Director - Americas, you will create the team, systems, service capability and operational foundations needed to deliver a seamless customer experience from order placement through clinical support and after-sales service. You will combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution, developing scalable processes that support growth while maintaining quality, compliance, efficiency and outstanding customer service.

**What You'll Do:**

* Establish and lead the operational infrastructure required for TASKA's direct-to-market strategy in the USA
* Develop scalable processes for customer onboarding, order fulfillment, training, support and service delivery
* Oversee logistics, warehousing, inventory management and distribution across the Americas
* Ensure operations meet relevant regulatory, quality and business requirements, working closely with TASKA's global Quality and Regulatory teams
* Establish operational KPIs and reporting frameworks to monitor service levels, customer satisfaction and business performance
* Identify operational risks and implement business continuity plans
* Drive continuous improvement to strengthen efficiency, customer experience and scalability
* Lead the United States repair and service function, ensuring timely, high-quality and compliant assessment, repair and return of TASKA devices
* Build, coach and develop a high-performing operations team with a strong culture of accountability, customer focus and continuous improvement
* Partner with the Commercial Director - Americas and teams across clinical services, customer support, sales and product management

card.title: Site Lab Operations Director
card.description:
Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

Abbott Rapid Diagnostics is part of Abbott’s Diagnostics family of businesses, bringing together exceptional teams of experts and industry leading technologies to support diagnostic testing which provides important information for treatment and management of diseases and other conditions.

The position of Site Lab Operations Director is within our Toxicology Business Unit located in Santa Rosa, California. The Site Lab Operations Director is responsible for the overall leadership, performance, and strategic direction of the Santa Rosa laboratory operation. The role has direct accountability for operational excellence, quality management system compliance, regulatory adherence, customer experience, employee engagement, and financial performance. The Director serves as the site leader responsible for ensuring all laboratory operations consistently meet applicable quality, regulatory, accreditation, and corporate requirements while delivering superior customer outcomes. This leader owns the site Operations P&L, including productivity improvement, cost-reduction initiatives, resource optimization, and gross margin enhancement. The successful candidate will be a strong, inspirational, and collaborative leader who develops high-performing teams, fosters a culture of accountability and continuous improvement, and partners effectively across Commercial, Quality, Regulatory, Finance, IT, and corporate functions to achieve business objectives.

This job description will be reviewed periodically and is subject to change by management.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Leadership Expectation**

* Provide visible, inspirational leadership that promotes accountability, engagement, collaboration, and a culture of continuous improvement.
* Accountable for achievement of customer experience, turnaround time, reporting accuracy and operational performance commitments.
* Develop and retain high-performing leaders through coaching, mentoring, succession planning, and talent development.
* Create an inclusive environment that encourages innovation, cross-functional partnership, and effective problem-solving.
* Serve as a key member of the Site Leadership Team and actively contribute to site strategy, business planning, and organizational effectiveness.

**Quality and Compliance Leadership**

* Own site compliance with all applicable quality, regulatory, accreditation, and company requirements, including CLIA (Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments), CAP (College of American Pathologists), FDA (Food and Drug Administration), state, and corporate quality standards, as applicable.
* Accountable for site quality performance and ensuring quality objectives are integrated into daily operations, business planning and strategic decision-making.
* Ensure laboratory operating procedures, policies, work instructions, and quality documentation are maintained, compliant, validated, and consistently executed.
* Partner closely with Quality and Regulatory Affairs to establish and sustain a culture of quality, compliance, and operational excellence.
* Champion right-first-time execution and drive sustainable improvements in quality, turnaround time, customer satisfaction, and operational reliability.

**Financial & Operations Leadership**

* Own the Operations P&L and overall laboratory financial performance, with direct accountability for COGS, productivity, labor efficiency, material utilization, capital deployment, and operating expense management.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans and budgets that support business growth and profitability objectives.
* Drive continuous productivity and cost-transformation initiatives that reduce COGS, improve gross margin, optimize labor efficiency and enhance operational scalability while maintaining compliance, quality, service levels, and employee engagement.
* Identify and implement process improvements, automation opportunities, and Lean/Six Sigma initiatives that improve efficiency and expand margins.
* Responsible for multiple operations functions supporting the facilities at the site (such as EHS, Facilities, Procurement, Shipping & Receiving, etc.).
* Ensure a safe and professional work environment consistent with OSHA requirements and company policies.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS | EDUCATION:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Natural Sciences, Forensic Toxicology or related field, or an equivalent combination of education and work experience.
* Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible work experience and proven success as an operations leader
* Significant experience in identifying and driving operational change and excellence.
* Prior experience with rules and regs of laboratory accrediting bodies such as CLIA, CAP, FDA, etc.

* Strong leadership skills, including the ability to set goals, and provide positive and constructive feedback respectfully to build positive relationships and improve business results.
* Ability to work effectively within a team in a fast-paced, changing environment.
* Strong verbal and written communications with ability to effectively communicate at multiple levels in the organization.
* undefined

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Master’s Degree, preferably science related.
* Prior supervisory experience in a large volume laboratory setting, either clinical or forensics with at least 20 or more direct reports.

* Sound knowledge of regulatory standards and good laboratory practices
* Eligible for RTI Responsible Person designation
* Significant experience leading and implementing OpEx/Six Sigma initiatives
* Preferred experience in toxicology laboratory
* Multi-tasks, prioritizes and meets deadlines in timely manner

* Demonstrated experience leading Quality Management Systems in a regulated laboratory, medical device, diagnostics, pharmaceutical, or healthcare environment.
* Proven ownership of operational P&L performance, including COGS management, budget development, productivity improvement, and margin expansion.
* Experience leading organizations through regulatory inspections, accreditation assessments, and external audits.
* Track record of driving large-scale transformational change, cost optimization, and operational excellence initiatives.
* Demonstrated ability to build, inspire, and lead high-performing cross-functional teams through periods of growth and change

The base pay for this position is $172,000.00 – $344,000.00. In specific locations, the pay range may vary from the range posted.

card.description:
**Job Description**
**Description & Requirements**
**About AESC US LLC**
AESC is a global leader in the development and manufacturing of high-performance batteries for zero-emission electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Founded in Japan in 2007 and headquartered in Yokohama, AESC has been building manufacturing capabilities around the world in the U.S., U.K., Europe, Japan and China to serve key markets and leading customers locally for over 14 years. Today, AESC has become the partner of choice for the world's leading OEMs and energy storage providers in North America, Europe, and Asia. Its advanced technology powers over one million electric vehicles and provides more than 15GWh of installed capacity for battery energy systems in over 60 countries.
 
 
AESC is expanding its footprint in the United States, and the Blythewood Repack Operation supports the broader South Carolina production network. AESC is committed to our local communities where it is making its investments, creating jobs, and supporting local charities.
 
 
**About The Role**
The Senior Operations Manager provides comprehensive leadership of manufacturing operations, driving safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective production. This role is responsible for integrating production execution with workforce planning, material flow, equipment availability, quality performance, and operational readiness.
 
 
The successful candidate must possess a broad understanding of plant operations and demonstrate the ability to lead across functions rather than operate solely as a production manager.
 
 
****What You Will Do****

* Direct daily manufacturing operations across assigned shifts and production areas.
* Establish and execute production plans that align labor, equipment, materials, and customer delivery requirements.
* Manage operational KPIs including throughput, OEE, labor productivity, downtime, scrap, cost, and on-time delivery.
* Collaborate with Maintenance and Engineering to ensure equipment availability, preventive maintenance execution, and effective downtime response.
* Partner with Quality to manage manufacturing defects, process compliance, containment, and corrective actions.
* Coordinate with Supply Chain and Logistics to maintain effective material flow, inventory accuracy, and production readiness.
* Lead production supervisors and team leaders, establishing clear expectations for attendance, timekeeping, staffing, overtime controls, and employee performance.
* Manage operating expenses, labor utilization, and production resource requirements.
* Promote a disciplined safety culture with EHS and enforce manufacturing operating standards.
* Support commissioning, production ramp-up, process stabilization, and future plant expansion.
* Develop staffing, succession, and workforce capability plans.
* Complete other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**
****What You Need****

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline, or equivalent substantial manufacturing leadership experience.
* At least 10 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including five years in plant operations leadership.
* Demonstrated accountability for manufacturing performance, staffing, safety, cost, and cross-functional execution.
* Experience with ERP/MES systems, Lean manufacturing, and operational performance management.

****What is "Nice to Have"?****

* Automotive OEM or Tier 1 experience.
* Battery manufacturing experience.
* High-volume automated manufacturing experience.
* Plant launch or greenfield ramp-up experience.

****Travel Requirements****
20% International Travel
 
 
****What We Offer****
Welcome to AESC, where you'll have the opportunity to tackle the world's most fascinating challenges alongside exceptionally talented individuals who are driven to make a difference. We strive to ensure that our employees are well taken care of, enabling them to focus on their work and contribute to our collective mission.
 
 
**We Offer**

* Comprehensive compensation packages including a competitive salary and a rewarding bonus program.
* An inclusive and diverse work environment that fosters and encourages professional and personal development.
* Highly automated, clean, safe, and temperature-controlled production environment.
* Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance.
* HSA and Flexible Spending Accounts.
* 401K with company match.
* Life Insurance (Company paid and additional voluntary life available).
* Paid Vacation and 14 Paid Holidays.
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage (Company Paid).
* Tuition reimbursement.

****Equal Employment Opportunity****
At AESC, we are committed to providing Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) to all individuals. We participate in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. Join us in our passion to design, manufacture, and sell high-performance products, contributing to a sustainable and zero-carbon emission future.
 
 
****Physical Requirements****
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable otherwise qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.
 
 

* Ability to stand, walk, and work on a concrete production floor for extended periods of time.
* Ability to read, write, speak, hear; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach and lift with hands and arms frequently throughout the day.
* Ability to wear all required PPE when working on the production floor.
* Required to occasionally lift, push, pull and/or move up to 10 pounds, and occasionally required to lift, push, pull and/or move up to 35 pounds.

****Work Environment****
The work environment is primarily a semi-automated/automated plant with a concrete floor and is characterized as climate controlled, moderate noise, and forklift traffic. The individual must be able to perform all essential functions as appropriate on the plant floor, in meetings, and with employees, management, customers and suppliers.
 
 
Candidate must perform the essential duties and responsibilities with or without reasonable accommodation efficiently and accurately, and without causing significant safety threat to self or others. The statements made herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this job classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive and inclusive list of all responsibilities, duties, and/or skills required of personnel so classified.
 
 
Hiring is contingent upon successful completion of a drug screen and background check, and verification of the candidate's eligibility to work in the United States. AESC US LLC is a drug-free workplace.

card.description:
The short version

Cenfire makes a new kind of switch: an all-silicon MEMS switch, built on a CMOS-compatible silicon spring instead of the metal springs of the past. Our first product, CF2140, is a signal and measurement switch for semiconductor test. It is finishing qualification now, and our second product starts qualification right behind it.

Making a product that works is one thing. Making it on schedule and at cost, month after month, through outside fabs, packaging and test houses, is another. We need the person who builds that machine. You will write the production ramp plan, get it approved, and then own it: wafer starts, packaging, test, inventory, second sources, distribution and customer shipment, for more than one product at a time.

What you will do

**Own the ramp plan.**
 In your first 90 days, map the CF2140 flow from wafer starts to shipment, set baselines for yield, cycle time and on-time delivery, and write the production ramp plan for CEO approval. After that, the plan and its results are yours.

**Run the weekly build plan.**
 Coordinate fab, packaging, test and shipments across every product in qualification or production. Assign owners and recovery dates when lots slip or material runs short. Commit to customers only what the plan can support.

**Run overlapping ramps.**
 Plan the second product's qualification builds alongside the first product's production ramp. Share wafers, test capacity and people between them deliberately, not by accident.

**Build the supply chain.**
 Manage our fab, packaging and test partners. Find and qualify second sources for the steps that carry the most risk. Set up the distribution channel that will serve our smaller customers.

**Build the operating system.**
 Lot traceability, ERP and MRP transactions, inventory accuracy and shipment reporting that people can trust.

**Lead through others, then build a team.**
 You start with no direct reports. You will work through Cenfire's engineering, quality and test staff, setting clear owners and deadlines. As volume grows, you will build the operations team, and some existing staff may move under you.

What you bring

**Required**

* You have personally taken a semiconductor, MEMS or comparable hardware product from qualification or pilot builds into repeatable production.
* You have planned across external wafer fabrication, packaging and test: yield loss, minimum lot sizes, lead times and constrained capacity.
* You have owned procurement, inventory, production scheduling, logistics and supplier performance, and you have implemented or improved ERP or MRP workflows.
* You make build and sourcing decisions from yield by stage and cost per good unit.
* You can lead people who don't report to you, and you can explain trade-offs plainly to engineering, quality, sales and the CEO.
* A degree in engineering, manufacturing or supply chain, or equivalent practical experience.

**Strongly preferred**

* You have run more than one product through overlapping qualification and production ramps.
* You have qualified second sources for fab, packaging or test.
* You have set up or worked with distributors.

  behind a new switching platform, with direct ownership of production scale and customer delivery.

* **You work directly with the CEO**
  and a small founding team.

* Reports to Seena Partokia, CEO.
* Stock options with 4-year vesting and a 1-year cliff.
* Base salary $160,000 to $180,000.
* We do not sponsor work visas or provide relocation assistance.

card.description:
**SEDIVER**

Sediver is a global leader in overhead line insulator technology, with decades of proven excellence in research, engineering, manufacturing, and field performance. With millions of insulators operating worldwide, Sediver is recognized for unmatched technical expertise, product reliability, and continuous innovation. As an industry pioneer, Sediver is actively shaping the future of more resilient, efficient, and reliable transmission and distribution networks.

With 6 commercial offices (China, France, Italy, Brazil, USA and Canada) and 4 production facilities in Italy, USA, Czech and China, the Group is highly international.

Sediver USA is in a period of sustained growth, with expanding demand across the U.S. and broader Americas grid modernization market. This trajectory creates a meaningful opportunity for Operations to scale capacity, professionalize systems, and shape the manufacturing footprint that will support the next decade of expansion.

**Position Summary:**

The Vice President of Operations is a senior executive leader accountable for setting and executing the operational strategy for Sediver USA and, in partnership with the President and Group COO, contributing to the broader Americas operational agenda. The role oversees the West Memphis, Arkansas manufacturing site — a 24/7 facility with end-to-end responsibility for production, quality, supply chain, and logistics.

This is a thought-partner role to the President of Sediver USA: the company is looking for a leader who can think beyond day-to-day plant execution and help shape how Operations enables Sediver’s long-term growth in the Americas.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Operations & Manufacturing Leadership**

* Champion a strong safety culture and ensure full compliance with safety standards, regulatory requirements, and internal procedures across all shifts.
* Set and execute the operational strategy for the U.S. site, aligning capacity, capability, and footprint with company growth plans across the Americas.
* Own factory performance against volume, quality, cost, and delivery commitments for continuous 24/7 operations.
* Define operational KPIs and governance routines that drive transparency, accountability, and timely corrective action.
* Build workforce planning and capability models that support both current production and future expansion.
* Partner with the President and Group COO as a strategic thought partner on industrial direction, investment priorities, and the broader Americas operational agenda.

**Quality & Technical Assurance (including HV Laboratory)**

* Provide executive oversight of the Quality organization and ensure quality is embedded at every stage of manufacturing.
* Drive structured problem-solving — root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, and durable resolution — so issues are caught before they reach customers.
* Oversee the High Voltage Laboratory and testing activities, ensuring technical rigor, standards compliance, and alignment with production and customer needs.
* Advance quality systems, controls, audits, and certifications in line with Sediver and industry standards.

**Supply Chain & Logistics**

* Lead Supply Chain, Logistics, and Inventory management through the Director of Supply Chain.
* Align production planning, material availability, inventory, and customer delivery commitments — and stress-test that alignment against growth scenarios.
* Drive cost control, vendor performance, and supply continuity without compromising quality or compliance.
* Ensure SAP and supporting systems accurately reflect inventory, production status, and logistics flows.

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Industrial, or Mechanical Engineering strongly preferred.
* MBA preferred.
* Proven senior leadership experience in complex industrial manufacturing environments, ideally including responsibility for a 24/7 site and exposure to multi-site or regional strategy.
* Willing to travel within the region and internationally as the role requires.
* Fluent in English (written and spoken).

**Key Competencies:**

* A leader who sets the operational strategy and can also walk the floor — credible with executives, customers, and operators alike.
* Strong ownership: takes accountability for outcomes, surfaces issues early with root cause and a path forward, and operates with a “no surprises” mindset.
* Decisive under pressure, comfortable making timely calls with imperfect information and adjusting as new information arrives.
